thread:
emma: quick heads-up — after the key rotation some iOS clients that only send `x-api-key` are getting 401s. it started happening after 03:00 deploy. anyone seen similar?
omar: we still accept `x-api-key` as a legacy fallback. auth precedence is: `Authorization: Bearer` -> `x-api-key` -> session cookie. if none valid -> 401.
leigh: curious why a few calls return 403 instead of 401 though — same key, same payload.
omar: 403 means the credential is valid but not authorized for the requested project/org. e.g., key scoped to org:org-a + request contained `x-project-id: proj-b` -> 403 (forbidden). if `x-project-id` absent we try to infer project from the key and that can succeed.
nathan: clarification: when both `Authorization` and `x-api-key` are present we ignore `x-api-key`, and if they mismatch we return 401 to avoid privilege escalation.
emma: ah okay. also, during rotation are both keys allowed for a while?
omar: yes — we have a configurable grace window (currently 120s) where both old+new are accepted unless the old one was explicitly revoked. revocation is immediate.
leigh: sdk note: older SDKs only send `x-api-key`. should we push a client update to prefer `Authorization`?
nathan: we planned that. docs/examples will be updated to `Authorization: Bearer` as the recommended pattern. older clients will keep working until we deprecate the fallback.
emma: can we return machine-friendly error codes in the body? like { "error": "forbidden", "reason": "project_mismatch" } rather than just a free-text message.
omar: we already include an `error.code` and `error.reason` in JSON for 401/403 but it's not documented. add it to the docs ticket.
leigh: also proposal: add a response warning header when fallback used: `Warning: x-api-key deprecated; use Authorization` so integrators spot it during rotation.
oman: +1 (typo: omar meant +1)
emma: small runtime ask: when `x-project-id` header is present we validate it against both token and key; if header points to a project outside the key's org should we 403 or try org fallback? i'd say 403 — explicit header beats inference.
omar: agreed — explicit header must be authoritative, so 403 on mismatch.
emma: thinking about tests: can SRE add an automated smoke check post-rotation that asserts: 1) no auth -> 401, 2) valid key wrong project -> 403, 3) old key in grace window -> 200, 4) revoked key -> 401.
devops-bot: New ticket created: #INF-8817 "Auth fallback + rotation smoke tests + docs updates" assigned to @emma, @omar, @nathan — due 2026-03-26.
emma: thanks — i'll update the dev docs (include the curl examples) and add a note about the `/auth/introspect` endpoint we want to add to validate key<->project mapping.
nathan: example curl for recommended pattern:
```bash
curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TOKEN" -H "x-project-id: proj-42" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
and legacy:
```bash
curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "x-api-key: $LEGACY_KEY" -H "x-project-id: proj-42" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
emma: perfect. leaving this thread — i'll link the ticket in the docs PR once created :thumbsup:
